domain_label: Agent Graph Topologies & Routing (Multi-Agent / Multi-Model Orchestration subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is orchestration topology and routing; agent training internals are out of scope
specialist agents are fine-tuned LLMs or specialized models; generalist is a frontier LLM
latency and cost models are pre-calibration estimates requiring staging measurement to refine
security threat model assumes LLM output is untrusted by default at agent boundaries
exclusions: embedding model training for vector memory

competency_questions.question: What graph topology (DAG, cyclic, hierarchical, any-to-any) is used and what are the termination conditions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GRAPH_DESIGN and HIER_ORCH define topology and termination policy

competency_questions.question: How is the topology evaluated and what metrics govern topology selection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOPO_EVAL defines ablation method and metric suite

competency_questions.question: What routing mechanism is used to dispatch tasks to agent nodes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTER_DESIGN defines routing mechanism options and selection criteria

competency_questions.question: How is conditional and dynamic dispatch implemented and how are branches bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COND_DISPATCH defines branch predicates and fan-out bounds

competency_questions.question: When does a specialist agent genuinely outperform a generalist and how is that measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPEC_BEAT defines evaluation method and net value calculation

competency_questions.question: How does MoE gating select experts and prevent expert collapse?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOE_GATING defines top-K selection and load balance mechanism

competency_questions.question: How are edge weights and confidence scores assigned and used for aggregation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EDGE_WEIGHT defines weight assignment and aggregation policy

competency_questions.question: How are loops detected and terminated in cyclic agent graphs?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOOP_CTRL defines cycle detection and termination conditions

competency_questions.question: How is hierarchical orchestration structured and what is the delegation protocol?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HIER_ORCH defines meta-orchestrator and sub-orchestrator scope

competency_questions.question: How are parallel agent executions synchronized and what happens if a branch fails?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PARALLEL_EXEC defines fork/join and FAULT_TOL defines branch failure handling

competency_questions.question: How are conflicting agent outputs detected and resolved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFLICT_RES defines conflict detection and arbitration policy

competency_questions.question: How is shared state managed and what are the memory tiers for long-horizon agents?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STATE_MGMT and MEMORY_ARCH define state schema and memory tiers

competency_questions.question: How is end-to-end latency and token cost modeled and budgeted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORCH_LATENCY and COST_BOUND define budget model and enforcement

competency_questions.question: What security isolation boundaries and fault tolerance mechanisms protect the agent graph?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SECURITY_ISO and FAULT_TOL define privilege boundaries and fault handling

glossary.definition: directed acyclic graph; agent execution graph with no cycles; enables topological sort and static analysis
mixture-of-experts gating mechanism that selects top-K specialist agents per token/task using learned weights
agent graph where arbitrary directed edges connect any pair of agents, not limited to series or parallel structures
graph edge with a scalar confidence or value weight used to blend or prioritize contributions from source agent
total wall-clock latency attributable to routing, state management, and aggregation overhead beyond individual agent inference time
MoE failure mode where the gating function routes all or most tokens to one expert, making other experts idle
fault tolerance pattern that stops routing to a degraded agent after threshold failures, preventing cascade failures
explicit separation of agent access rights to shared state or external tools based on trust level and task scope
latency and token cost added by the routing mechanism to invoke a specialist agent versus a single generalist call

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for agent graph topology and orchestration work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Wooldridge MAS, Shoham & Leyton-Brown, Russell & Norvig AIMA, Shazeer et al. 2017 MoE, Fedus et al. 2021 Switch Transformer
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Wooldridge 2002 An Introduction to MultiAgent Systems; Shoham & Leyton-Brown 2008 Multiagent Systems; Russell & Norvig 2021 AIMA 4th ed; Shazeer et al. 2017 Outrageously Large Neural Networks; Fedus et al. 2021 Switch Transformers

nodes.definition: Design the agent execution graph: choose DAG vs cyclic topology, define node roles, edge semantics, and termination conditions for the multi-agent workflow.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task complexity or routing logic changes materially

pros.claim: Explicit graph spec enables static analysis and loop detection before runtime
pros.example: DAG topological sort catches dependency cycles at deploy time

pros.claim: Separates orchestration logic from individual agent code
pros.example: swap agent without rewiring topology

cons.claim: Upfront graph design may lag dynamic task requirements
cons.example: hard-coded DAG fails when subtask count is data-dependent

failure_modes: cycles without termination guards cause infinite loops
over-connected graphs amplify latency
acceptance_tests: all cycles have explicit break conditions
graph is serializable to JSON schema
revisit_triggers: task complexity changes requiring topology refactor

nodes.definition: Design the router/dispatcher that reads task state and routes to the next agent node; covers rule-based, classifier-based, and LLM-judge routers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: routing accuracy degrades or new agent specialties added

pros.claim: Correct routing is prerequisite to specialist accuracy gains
pros.example: coding task routed to writing agent negates specialization benefit

pros.claim: Rule-based routers are interpretable and fast; classifier routers generalize to novel inputs
pros.example: regex router 0ms latency vs 200ms LLM judge

cons.claim: LLM-judge router adds round-trip cost per dispatch; compounds in deep graphs
cons.example: 5-hop DAG with 200ms router per hop adds 1s overhead

failure_modes: router misclassifies task type causing wrong specialist invocation
LLM-judge router adds latency proportional to judge model size
acceptance_tests: router accuracy >=0.90 on held-out task type benchmark
fallback path tested for every route
revisit_triggers: new agent added requiring route coverage

nodes.definition: Implement MoE gating to select top-K specialist agents per token or task chunk; covers softmax gating, top-K selection, load balancing, and auxiliary loss to prevent expert collapse (Shazeer 2017, Fedus 2021).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: expert collapse metrics trigger or new gating architecture published

pros.claim: Top-K gating enables parallel specialist execution reducing latency vs serial routing
pros.example: top-2 gating fires two experts simultaneously then merges

pros.claim: Auxiliary load-balance loss prevents winner-take-all collapse proven in Switch Transformer
pros.example: Fedus et al. 2021: capacity factor with balance loss maintains utilization

cons.claim: Discrete top-K selection is non-differentiable; requires auxiliary loss or straight-through estimator
cons.example: gradient does not flow through argmax expert selection

failure_modes: expert collapse: one expert handles all tokens
load imbalance saturates some agents and idles others
gating instability during online updates
acceptance_tests: expert utilization variance <0.15 across experts
auxiliary load-balance loss coefficient validated
revisit_triggers: expert collapse detected by utilization monitor

nodes.definition: Assign and maintain value/confidence weights on graph edges to enable weighted aggregation, priority dispatch, and dynamic re-weighting during execution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: quality distribution of agents shifts materially

pros.claim: Confidence-weighted edges enable soft routing and result blending without hard commits
pros.example: two agents answer; weights 0.7/0.3 blend their outputs proportionally

cons.claim: Weight maintenance overhead grows O(E) with edge count in dense graphs
cons.example: 1000-edge graph requires 1000 weight updates per quality event

failure_modes: stale weights misrepresent current agent quality
circular weight updates cause oscillation
acceptance_tests: edge weight updates are monotonically bounded
aggregation tested with adversarial low-confidence inputs

nodes.definition: Implement loop guards and termination criteria for cyclic agent graphs: max-iteration caps, convergence checks, confidence thresholds, and timeout budgets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: runaway loops observed in staging or convergence criteria revised

pros.claim: Hard max-iter cap prevents unbounded cost in adversarial or buggy scenarios
pros.example: reflexion-style self-critique loops capped at 5 iters to bound cost

cons.claim: Fixed iteration cap may terminate before convergence on legitimately long tasks
cons.example: complex reasoning cuts off at cap before reaching correct answer

failure_modes: runaway loop from missing base case
oscillation between two states that never converges
timeout too short discards valid intermediate results
acceptance_tests: all cycles terminate within configured max_iter on all test inputs
timeout fires before resource exhaustion
revisit_triggers: new cycle type added to graph

nodes.definition: Implement conditional branching and dynamic dispatch in agent graphs: if/else branches, switch-case dispatch, and runtime-determined fan-out based on intermediate results.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new branch predicates added or fan-out limits revised

pros.claim: Dynamic dispatch enables data-dependent specialization unreachable by static routing
pros.example: routing to medical vs legal specialist based on intermediate entity detection result

cons.claim: Dynamic branching makes execution traces non-deterministic and hard to debug
cons.example: same input produces different branch path on retry due to stochastic upstream

failure_modes: branch predicate based on stale state
fan-out explosion creating O(2^n) agent invocations
untested branches taken only in production
acceptance_tests: all branches exercised in integration tests
fan-out bounded by explicit max_branches config

nodes.definition: Execute multiple agent nodes in parallel (fan-out) and synchronize results: fork/join patterns, async invocation, and result barrier synchronization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: async runtime changes or branch failure modes emerge in production

pros.claim: Parallel execution reduces wall-clock latency proportionally to independent branches
pros.example: 3 independent agents in parallel: 1x latency instead of 3x serial

cons.claim: Resource cost is additive over parallel branches; latency saving may not justify token cost
cons.example: 3x parallel invocations triple GPU inference cost for same wall-clock win

failure_modes: join hangs when one branch fails silently
result ordering non-determinism breaks downstream
resource contention at join point
acceptance_tests: join barrier has timeout
failed branch triggers fallback not hang
result ordering is deterministic
revisit_triggers: agent count at fan-out exceeds resource budget

nodes.definition: Aggregate results from multiple agent branches: voting, weighted averaging, confidence-based selection, and LLM-synthesizer patterns.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: aggregation quality degrades or new conflict pattern identified

pros.claim: Voting and confidence-weighted averaging improve robustness over single-agent results
pros.example: majority vote across 3 agents reduces individual error rate

cons.claim: Aggregation adds latency for serial synthesis; synthesis LLM may introduce new errors
cons.example: LLM synthesizer merges two correct answers into incorrect hybrid

failure_modes: conflicting outputs with no resolution policy
confidence collapse when all branches low-confidence
LLM synthesizer hallucinating merged content
acceptance_tests: aggregation output passes consistency check against inputs
tie-breaking policy documented and tested
revisit_triggers: new branch type added requiring new merge strategy

nodes.definition: Design shared state store for multi-agent workflows: context object schema, read/write access patterns, state mutation ordering, and conflict resolution for concurrent writes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: concurrent write conflicts observed or state schema evolves

pros.claim: Shared state enables information reuse across agent hops without re-querying
pros.example: extracted entities stored once, read by all downstream agents

pros.claim: Explicit state schema prevents silent context corruption between agents
pros.example: typed state object catches field name mismatches at parse time

cons.claim: Shared mutable state introduces concurrency bugs in parallel execution paths
cons.example: two parallel agents append to same list without lock, losing one result

failure_modes: concurrent writes corrupt shared state
state bloat exceeds context window of consumer agents
stale reads from cached state
acceptance_tests: concurrent writes are serialized or CAS-protected
state size bounded by schema validation
revisit_triggers: new agent added with write access

nodes.definition: Model and budget end-to-end latency and token cost for the agent graph: hop count, routing overhead, parallel speedup, and compounding effects across edges.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: SLA violations observed or topology changes materially

pros.claim: Upfront latency modeling prevents architecture choices that fail SLA at scale
pros.example: 5-hop LLM router chain modeled at design time reveals 5s p95 latency exceeding 2s SLA

cons.claim: Latency models require calibration data from real deployments; pre-launch estimates are rough
cons.example: model predicts 1.2s; production shows 1.8s due to cold-start and network variance

failure_modes: critical path miscalculated ignoring routing overhead
latency budget set without token cost consideration
parallelism assumed without accounting for join latency
acceptance_tests: latency model validated against staging measurements
cost projection within 15% of actual

nodes.definition: Design fault-tolerance mechanisms: per-node retry policies, circuit breakers, fallback agent paths, and partial-result recovery in agent graphs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production failure events reveal gaps in retry/fallback coverage

pros.claim: Circuit breakers prevent cascade failures in tightly-coupled agent graphs
pros.example: unhealthy math agent isolated; router diverts to fallback within one failed request

pros.claim: Fallback paths maintain service continuity at degraded quality rather than total failure
pros.example: specialized coder agent down; fallback to generalist preserves response

cons.claim: Retries amplify load on already-degraded agents; fallback quality may be unacceptable
cons.example: 3 retries triple load on flapping agent before circuit breaks

failure_modes: retry storms when upstream agent flaps
fallback agent lower quality degrades user experience
circuit breaker opens prematurely on transient errors
acceptance_tests: retry policy has exponential backoff with jitter
circuit breaker thresholds tested in chaos experiments
revisit_triggers: new agent failure mode observed in production

nodes.definition: Instrument multi-agent graphs for observability: distributed tracing across agent hops, execution DAG replay, latency attribution, and anomaly alerting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: trace gaps or attribution ambiguity identified in incident postmortem

pros.claim: Distributed tracing is prerequisite to diagnosing latency regressions in multi-hop graphs
pros.example: trace shows router hop adds 350ms; identified as cause of SLA violation

cons.claim: High-cardinality traces add storage and overhead; sampling risks missing rare failure paths
cons.example: 1% sample misses the one execution path that errors in production

failure_modes: trace context lost across async agent boundaries
trace volume overwhelms storage
attribution ambiguous when multiple agents contribute to output
acceptance_tests: trace coverage >=95% of agent invocations
end-to-end trace reconstructable for any execution
revisit_triggers: new agent added without trace instrumentation

nodes.definition: Decide whether a specialized agent node genuinely outperforms a generalist LLM on the target subtask; apply empirical evaluation to justify routing overhead of specialist invocation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: base model version increments or production task distribution shifts materially

pros.claim: Specialist advantage is narrow and task-distribution-dependent; must be measured not assumed
pros.example: fine-tuned coder beats GPT-4 on HumanEval but loses on open-domain coding questions

pros.claim: Routing overhead is a real cost that must be netted against accuracy gain
pros.example: 2% accuracy gain with 300ms added latency is net negative for real-time chat

cons.claim: Goodhart effect: specialist tuned on benchmark may overfit, losing edge on real traffic
cons.example: SFT on HumanEval test-set contamination inflates score without real gain

failure_modes: specialist wins on benchmark but loses on real traffic distribution
generalist improved by new model release making specialist redundant
evaluation on narrow benchmark that does not represent production distribution
acceptance_tests: specialist evaluated on held-out production task sample not benchmark
routing overhead cost subtracted from accuracy gain to compute net value

nodes.definition: Evaluate alternative graph topologies via ablation: compare serial, parallel, hierarchical, and any-to-any variants on quality, latency, and cost metrics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: quality metrics disagree or new topology variant proposed

pros.claim: Empirical ablation prevents committing to intuitive but suboptimal topology
pros.example: assumed parallel beats serial; ablation shows serial with caching wins on cost

cons.claim: Ablation cost is O(N_topologies * eval_cost); prohibitive for large agent graphs
cons.example: evaluating 5 topologies with 1000 examples costs 5x evaluation budget

failure_modes: ablation uses different agent quality across topologies making comparison invalid
evaluation metrics disagree on best topology
acceptance_tests: ablation holds agent quality constant across topology variants
all evaluation metrics reported not just cherry-picked winner

nodes.definition: Design hierarchical orchestration: meta-orchestrator decomposes tasks and dispatches to sub-orchestrators that manage specialist agent clusters.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task complexity tier changes or delegation failures observed

pros.claim: Hierarchy enables scalability beyond flat graph limits by partitioning routing responsibility
pros.example: meta-orchestrator routes to domain clusters; domain orchestrators route to specialists

pros.claim: Clear scope boundaries at each level reduce coupling and enable independent testing
pros.example: math cluster tested independently of writing cluster

cons.claim: Hierarchy adds latency at each delegation level; deep hierarchies compound orchestration overhead
cons.example: 3-level hierarchy: 3x routing overhead even for simple tasks

failure_modes: meta-orchestrator overloads itself by not delegating
scope boundary between orchestration levels ambiguous
sub-orchestrator quality invisible to meta-level
acceptance_tests: delegation scope boundaries formally specified
meta-orchestrator tested for over-centralization pattern

nodes.definition: Enable and govern arbitrary any-to-any directed edges in the agent graph including non-local skip connections, feedback edges, and cross-cluster edges beyond simple series/parallel structures.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new cross-cluster edge request or cycle detected in graph validation

pros.claim: Any-to-any edges enable feedback loops and skip connections that series/parallel topology cannot express
pros.example: evaluator agent sends feedback directly to any upstream agent without routing through meta-orchestrator

pros.claim: Edge permission matrix prevents unauthorized cross-cluster edges that violate security or quality boundaries
pros.example: external-facing agent cannot send to internal data-access agent without policy approval

cons.claim: Dense any-to-any graphs are exponentially harder to reason about than DAGs
cons.example: N=20 agents with any-to-any edges: up to 380 possible directed edges to audit

failure_modes: uncontrolled any-to-any edges create undetectable cycles
edge explosion creates O(N^2) maintenance surface
skip connections bypass required validation nodes
acceptance_tests: edge permission matrix enforced at graph compile time
cycle detection passes on all registered edge sets
revisit_triggers: new agent pair requests direct edge

nodes.definition: Distribute task load across replicated specialist agent instances: load-aware routing, autoscaling triggers, and queue-based backpressure to prevent hotspot formation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: traffic pattern changes or hotspot alerts fire

pros.claim: Load-aware routing prevents hotspot formation that degrades tail latency
pros.example: round-robin replaced with queue-depth-weighted routing; p99 latency drops 40%

cons.claim: Autoscaling introduces cold-start latency for new agent instances; warm pool increases idle cost
cons.example: cold container start adds 10s latency spike on traffic burst

failure_modes: hotspot on single expert while others idle
autoscaling too slow to absorb traffic spike
queue backpressure propagates upstream causing router timeout
acceptance_tests: load distribution variance <20% across agent replicas under peak load test
autoscaling response time <30s
revisit_triggers: new agent type added with uneven load profile

nodes.definition: Enforce per-request and per-graph token and monetary cost budgets: budget accounting, early-stopping when budget exhausted, and cost-quality tradeoff decisions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pricing model changes or cost overrun events occur

pros.claim: Hard budget enforcement prevents runaway costs in adversarial or infinite-loop scenarios
pros.example: multi-agent debate loop with no budget cap costs 100x expected on complex inputs

cons.claim: Hard budget cuts may truncate reasoning mid-step returning unusable partial results
cons.example: budget fires after 3 of 5 required hops; output is incomplete draft

failure_modes: budget exhausted mid-graph returns partial result without signal
budget too tight eliminates necessary agent hops
cost tracking inaccurate due to batching
acceptance_tests: early-stop returns explicit partial_result signal not silent truncation
budget accounting accurate within 5% vs actual billing

nodes.definition: Design agent memory tiers: in-context window (ephemeral), external vector store (semantic), and structured KV store (episodic/persistent); govern what each agent writes and reads.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context window budget changes or retrieval precision drops

pros.claim: Tiered memory enables long-horizon agents that exceed single-context-window task length
pros.example: research agent stores intermediate findings in vector store; retrieves relevant subset per hop

cons.claim: External memory adds retrieval latency and retrieval error risk; in-context memory is simpler
cons.example: vector retrieval adds 50ms per hop and may return semantically similar but wrong memories

failure_modes: context window overflow silently truncates history
vector retrieval retrieves wrong memories contaminating agent
mixing in-context and external memory creates consistency gaps
acceptance_tests: context overflow handled explicitly not silently
vector retrieval precision >=0.80 on synthetic memory probe

nodes.definition: Resolve disagreements between agent outputs: detect conflicts, apply arbitration policies (judge agent, majority vote, human escalation), and document resolution rationale.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new conflict type observed or arbitration quality degrades

pros.claim: Explicit conflict resolution prevents silent answer corruption when agents disagree
pros.example: two agents give contradictory facts; judge agent resolves with citation

pros.claim: Documented resolution rationale enables post-hoc auditing of arbitration quality
pros.example: arbitration log shows judge agent correctly overrode incorrect minority agent

cons.claim: Judge agent arbitration adds latency and may propagate judge's own errors
cons.example: judge agent trained on same data distribution as conflicting agents; cannot resolve distributional disagreements

failure_modes: conflict undetected because outputs are semantically not lexically different
judge agent introduces its own bias into arbitration
human escalation volume too high to sustain
acceptance_tests: semantic conflict detection tested on known-conflicting output pairs
judge agent bias measured and bounded
revisit_triggers: new conflict type emerges in production

nodes.definition: Enforce security isolation between agents: privilege boundaries, prompt-injection defenses at agent interfaces, output sanitization before passing to downstream agents, and audit logging.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new attack vector identified or privilege boundary violated in incident

pros.claim: Agent-to-agent trust boundaries are necessary because LLM outputs are not sanitized by default
pros.example: external data summarizer injects instructions that redirect downstream code-executor agent

pros.claim: Output sanitization at agent boundaries prevents injection chain propagation
pros.example: strip control tokens from summarizer output before passing to planner agent

cons.claim: Sanitization may remove valid content; overly restrictive policies reduce agent utility
cons.example: aggressive HTML stripping removes valid structured data in agent outputs

failure_modes: prompt injection via tool output propagates across agent hops
over-privileged agent writes to state it should only read
audit log missing agent invocations outside primary path
acceptance_tests: injection defense tested with known attack payloads
privilege boundaries enforced by policy not convention
revisit_triggers: new agent added with different privilege tier

nodes.definition: Version and migrate agent graphs: schema versioning for graph topology, backward-compatible agent interface changes, and migration playbooks for topology upgrades.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: topology migration planned or rollback executed in production

pros.claim: Schema versioning enables safe incremental topology upgrades without full system downtime
pros.example: v2 graph deployed alongside v1; traffic gradually migrated with rollback option

cons.claim: Versioning adds schema management overhead; small teams may not need full versioning for early-stage systems
cons.example: startup with weekly topology changes finds versioning overhead exceeds migration cost

failure_modes: topology change breaks existing state objects mid-flight
rollback impossible without version history
schema drift between orchestrator and agents
acceptance_tests: schema version checked at agent handshake
rollback procedure tested in staging

edges.why_related: Router design derives from and depends on the graph topology specification
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Ensures routing logic matches actual graph edge capabilities
edges.risk_of_conflict: Router misconfigured if graph topology changes without router update
edges.example: DAG compiled before router rules are written

edges.why_related: Loop control guards must know which edges form cycles to configure termination
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables static cycle detection before runtime
edges.risk_of_conflict: Cycles without guards cause unbounded execution cost
edges.example: Cycle list extracted from graph adjacency spec to configure max-iter caps

edges.why_related: Edge weight schema depends on the graph edge definition
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows typed weight assignment per edge class
edges.risk_of_conflict: Weight system incomplete if graph adds new edge types
edges.example: Edge weight config references edge ids from GRAPH_DESIGN

edges.why_related: Parallel execution plan derived from independent branches in the graph
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Identifies which branches can safely execute concurrently
edges.risk_of_conflict: Parallelism assumption may be wrong if graph has hidden dependencies
edges.example: Fork/join plan built from topological independence analysis of graph

edges.why_related: State schema depends on what agents and edges exist in the graph
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Ensures state fields cover all agent information needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: State schema incomplete if graph expands without update
edges.example: State object fields derived from graph node interface contracts

edges.why_related: Any-to-any edge governance builds on the base graph topology definition
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows incremental addition of non-standard edges under policy control
edges.risk_of_conflict: Uncontrolled edges bypass topology constraints
edges.example: Edge permission matrix references base graph node registry

edges.why_related: Hierarchical orchestration design requires knowing the base graph structure to partition
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables logical clustering of nodes into sub-orchestrator scopes
edges.risk_of_conflict: Hierarchy boundaries may conflict with actual task dependencies in graph
edges.example: Sub-orchestrator scope boundaries drawn from graph connected components

edges.why_related: Graph versioning requires the graph spec to tag and track
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables reproducible topology snapshots for rollback
edges.risk_of_conflict: Without base graph spec, version diffs are ambiguous
edges.example: Version tag applied to signed-off GRAPH_DESIGN artifact

edges.why_related: MoE gating is a specialized routing mechanism built on the router design interface
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows MoE to reuse router fallback and monitoring infrastructure
edges.risk_of_conflict: MoE gating exposes routing complexity not present in simple classifiers
edges.example: MoE gating module satisfies the router interface contract

edges.why_related: Conditional dispatch is implemented as a subtype of the router mechanism
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Reuses router's agent pool registry and fallback policy
edges.risk_of_conflict: Conditional branches must be registered in router's routing table
edges.example: Branch predicates compiled into router dispatch table

edges.why_related: Specialist evaluation requires knowing the routing overhead of the router being evaluated against
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Grounds net-value calculation in actual routing cost
edges.risk_of_conflict: Specialist gain overstated if routing overhead excluded from cost model
edges.example: SPEC_BEAT subtracts measured router latency from specialist accuracy gain

edges.why_related: Load balancing extends the router to distribute load across replicated agents
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables router-aware load distribution without separate dispatch layer
edges.risk_of_conflict: Load balancer misconfigures routing weights if router interface changes
edges.example: Load balancer registered as a routing plugin in ROUTER_DESIGN infrastructure

edges.why_related: Aggregation uses edge confidence weights to blend results from multiple branches
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables weighted averaging without hardcoded branch priorities
edges.risk_of_conflict: Aggregation quality degrades if weights not maintained
edges.example: AGG_MERGE reads confidence weights from EDGE_WEIGHT registry per branch

edges.why_related: Aggregation is the join step that follows parallel fan-out execution
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Separates execution concerns from result fusion concerns
edges.risk_of_conflict: Aggregation cannot proceed until all parallel branches complete or timeout
edges.example: Join barrier in PARALLEL_EXEC signals AGG_MERGE when all results available

edges.why_related: Distributed tracing instruments state access events to reconstruct execution history
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables correlation of state mutations with agent execution traces
edges.risk_of_conflict: Trace incomplete without state access events
edges.example: State read/write operations emit trace events to OBS_TRACE collector

edges.why_related: Memory architecture extends the state store with tiered retrieval for long-horizon context
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows state overflow to external memory without agent-visible interface change
edges.risk_of_conflict: Memory tier routing inconsistency if STATE_MGMT schema changes
edges.example: Context overflow handled by MEMORY_ARCH overflow handler registered in STATE_MGMT

edges.why_related: State schema versioning requires base state schema from STATE_MGMT
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables migration scripts to translate state objects between versions
edges.risk_of_conflict: Version migration fails if state schema undocumented
edges.example: Schema version tag applied to STATE_MGMT schema artifact

edges.why_related: Conflict resolution activates when aggregation detects contradictory branch outputs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Separates conflict detection from conflict resolution logic
edges.risk_of_conflict: Conflicts silently merged without resolution if CONFLICT_RES not triggered
edges.example: AGG_MERGE calls CONFLICT_RES arbitration when semantic contradiction detected

edges.why_related: Fault tolerance retry policy must respect loop iteration budget to avoid cost explosion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Ensures retries counted against loop iteration cap
edges.risk_of_conflict: Retries within a loop can exceed max-iter cap without coordination
edges.example: FAULT_TOL retry counter shares budget with LOOP_CTRL iteration counter

edges.why_related: Any-to-any edge governance requires security isolation enforcement at non-standard edge crossings
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Ensures cross-trust-level edges have sanitization before use
edges.risk_of_conflict: Unchecked any-to-any edges enable injection chain attacks
edges.example: Edge permission matrix enforces SECURITY_ISO trust level check before edge registration

edges.why_related: MoE gating requires load balancing to prevent expert collapse from uneven routing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows utilization monitoring to feed back into gating weight adjustment
edges.risk_of_conflict: Expert collapse undetected without load balancer utilization metrics
edges.example: LOAD_BAL monitors per-expert utilization; feeds alert to MOE_GATING auxiliary loss tuner

edges.why_related: Cost budget requires latency model to estimate full-path token and monetary cost
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Grounds budget setting in modeled rather than guessed cost
edges.risk_of_conflict: Budget set too low or high without latency model calibration
edges.example: COST_BOUND budget = ORCH_LATENCY full-path cost estimate * budget_headroom_factor

edges.why_related: Latency model requires graph topology to compute hop count and critical path
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables SLA feasibility analysis before topology is committed
edges.risk_of_conflict: Latency model inaccurate if topology not finalized
edges.example: Critical path computed from GRAPH_DESIGN adjacency spec

edges.why_related: Router latency is a component of total orchestration latency that must be modeled
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Prevents underestimating orchestration overhead from routing steps
edges.risk_of_conflict: Router overhead excluded from model if not explicitly included
edges.example: ORCH_LATENCY adds router_latency term per routing hop in graph

edges.why_related: Topology evaluation requires specialist advantage measurements to score topology variants fairly
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows topology ablation to account for specialist quality when comparing topologies
edges.risk_of_conflict: Topology comparison invalid if specialist quality differs across variants
edges.example: TOPO_EVAL pins agent quality scores from SPEC_BEAT during ablation

edges.why_related: Topology evaluation requires latency model to compare topology variants on latency metric
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables fair latency comparison holding agent inference time constant
edges.risk_of_conflict: Topology latency comparison invalid without orchestration overhead model
edges.example: TOPO_EVAL uses ORCH_LATENCY model per topology variant

edges.why_related: Topology evaluation requires candidate topologies from GRAPH_DESIGN as ablation variants
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Provides structured topology representations for systematic comparison
edges.risk_of_conflict: Ablation lacks canonical topology representations without GRAPH_DESIGN artifacts
edges.example: TOPO_EVAL ablation set built from GRAPH_DESIGN topology variants

edges.why_related: Hierarchical orchestrators use conditional dispatch to delegate to sub-orchestrators
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows meta-orchestrator to apply task-type branching in delegation decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: Delegation logic duplicates routing logic if not reusing COND_DISPATCH
edges.example: Meta-orchestrator delegation implemented as conditional dispatch branch to sub-orchestrator

edges.why_related: MoE routing cost depends on how many experts are invoked; cost budget must account for K-expert cost
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Prevents K-expert parallel cost from exceeding single-agent budget unexpectedly
edges.risk_of_conflict: MoE cost underestimated if budget set for single agent call
edges.example: COST_BOUND budget includes K * expert_cost_per_token for MoE paths

edges.why_related: Parallel execution multiplies cost proportionally to branch count, conflicting with cost minimization
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Latency improvement from parallelism
edges.risk_of_conflict: Cost budget exceeded when parallel branches multiply token cost beyond budget
edges.example: 3 parallel branches triple inference cost vs serial
edges.resolution_rule: accept parallel execution only when latency savings exceed token cost increase per ORCH_LATENCY model

edges.why_related: Any-to-any feedback edges create cycles that conflict with termination requirements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Feedback edges enable iterative refinement
edges.risk_of_conflict: Any-to-any cycles without guards cause unbounded execution
edges.example: feedback edge from evaluator to planner creates cycle; needs max-iter cap
edges.resolution_rule: any-to-any edges forming cycles MUST have LOOP_CTRL guard; no exception

edges.why_related: MoE gating assumes specialist advantage but SPEC_BEAT may find no advantage on real traffic
edges.benefit_of_coupling: MoE enables parallel specialist execution
edges.risk_of_conflict: MoE routing overhead is wasted cost if specialist advantage is zero
edges.example: MoE deployed before SPEC_BEAT validation; specialist beats generalist on benchmark but not production
edges.resolution_rule: SPEC_BEAT must validate specialist advantage on production sample before MoE deployment

edges.why_related: Hierarchical delegation adds latency at each level conflicting with latency SLA
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Hierarchy enables modular reasoning and specialization
edges.risk_of_conflict: Deep hierarchy exceeds latency SLA from delegation overhead
edges.example: 3-level hierarchy adds 3x routing overhead even for simple tasks
edges.resolution_rule: ORCH_LATENCY model must gate hierarchy depth; reject if p95 exceeds SLA

edges.why_related: Retries amplify cost on degraded agents, conflicting with fixed cost budget
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Retries improve reliability and success rate
edges.risk_of_conflict: Retries exhaust budget before task completes
edges.example: 3 retries on 3-agent graph multiplies cost by 3x before circuit breaks
edges.resolution_rule: cost budget must reserve retry_budget_fraction; FAULT_TOL retry limit coordinated with COST_BOUND

edges.why_related: Security sanitization at parallel branch boundaries adds per-branch latency overhead
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Isolation prevents injection chain propagation
edges.risk_of_conflict: Sanitization overhead negates latency gains from parallelism
edges.example: 4 parallel branches each requiring sanitization adds 4x sanitization cost
edges.resolution_rule: accept sanitization overhead as non-negotiable; optimize sanitization cost not skip it

edges.why_related: Observability traces feed latency and failure data back to fault tolerance configuration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Production trace data improves retry and circuit breaker thresholds
edges.risk_of_conflict: Feedback loop creates update cycle that needs versioning
edges.example: Circuit breaker thresholds tuned from p99 failure rate observed in traces

edges.why_related: Production observability data feeds back to topology evaluation with real latency measurements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Calibrates topology evaluation model with production data
edges.risk_of_conflict: Feedback from production may invalidate topology decision requiring revision
edges.example: TOPO_EVAL re-run with production latency data from OBS_TRACE after 30-day production period

edges.why_related: Conflict resolution events are causally logged to observability for audit and quality analysis
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Enables post-hoc review of arbitration decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: Conflict arbitration quality unauditable without trace
edges.example: Every CONFLICT_RES arbitration event emits structured trace event with inputs and decision

edges.why_related: State access patterns causally determine privilege boundary requirements for security isolation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Ensures privilege boundaries are grounded in actual state access needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: Privilege boundaries misconfigured if state access patterns not analyzed
edges.example: SECURITY_ISO privilege matrix derived from STATE_MGMT read/write access analysis

edges.why_related: Memory architecture feedback informs state management about overflow and retrieval performance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Allows state schema to adapt to memory tier pressure
edges.risk_of_conflict: Memory overflow handling policy misconfigured if state size patterns not observed
edges.example: MEMORY_ARCH overflow events trigger STATE_MGMT to adjust context budget allocation

conflict_axes.name: latency_vs_specialization_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: Adding specialist agents and routing hops reduces latency and increases cost; accuracy gains must be net-positive after overhead
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use ORCH_LATENCY model to compute net value; reject specialization when routing overhead exceeds accuracy gain

conflict_axes.name: any_to_any_flexibility_vs_graph_complexity
conflict_axes.description: Any-to-any edges enable rich topologies but increase audit surface and cycle risk exponentially with node count
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use edge permission matrix and cycle detection; default to DAG unless non-local edge provides proven value

conflict_axes.name: parallel_execution_cost_vs_latency
conflict_axes.description: Parallel fan-out reduces wall-clock latency but multiplies token and compute cost proportionally
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: only parallelize branches that are on critical path and where combined cost is within budget

conflict_axes.name: specialist_advantage_vs_goodhart_contamination
conflict_axes.description: Specialist fine-tuned on benchmark may show inflated scores due to contamination or Goodhart effect rather than real task gain
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: evaluate on held-out production task sample; subtract routing overhead from measured gain; revisit when base model updates

conflict_axes.name: shared_state_vs_isolation
conflict_axes.description: Shared mutable state enables information reuse but creates concurrency bugs and security risks when agents have different trust levels
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: partition state by trust level; use read-only views for lower-trust agents; serialize concurrent writes

conflict_axes.name: fault_tolerance_retry_vs_cost_amplification
conflict_axes.description: Retries improve reliability but amplify cost on degraded agents; cost budget must reserve headroom for retry budget
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap retry count in FAULT_TOL; reserve retry budget in COST_BOUND; use exponential backoff to bound cost

conflict_axes.name: hierarchy_depth_vs_delegation_latency
conflict_axes.description: Deeper orchestration hierarchies improve modularity but compound delegation latency at each level
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: limit hierarchy to 2-3 levels unless task complexity genuinely requires deeper decomposition; profile with ORCH_LATENCY

conflict_axes.name: moe_expert_capacity_vs_load_imbalance
conflict_axes.description: Increasing MoE expert capacity reduces token overflow but idle capacity wastes compute; balance factor required
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use auxiliary load-balance loss during training; monitor utilization distribution in production; adjust capacity factor

conflict_axes.name: observability_trace_volume_vs_storage_cost
conflict_axes.description: High-cardinality full traces enable complete debugging but incur significant storage and overhead cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use adaptive sampling: full trace for errors and SLA violations; sampled trace for normal traffic

conflict_axes.name: dynamic_routing_expressiveness_vs_determinism
conflict_axes.description: Dynamic/conditional dispatch enables data-dependent specialization but makes execution traces non-deterministic
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: log dispatch decisions with inputs; replay from log for debugging; add deterministic mode for testing

edge_cases.description: Expert collapse in MoE: one expert handles >90% of tokens; all others idle
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce auxiliary load-balance loss; monitor utilization per expert; add capacity factor constraint

edge_cases.description: Cycle without termination: any-to-any feedback edge creates unbounded loop consuming infinite tokens
edge_cases.trigger: cycle detected in graph with no loop guard
edge_cases.mitigation: cycle detection at graph compile time; hard max-iter cap on all cycles; cost budget circuit breaker

edge_cases.description: Specialist regression: base model update makes generalist competitive; specialist routing adds cost with no gain
edge_cases.trigger: base model increments; specialist benchmark delta shrinks below routing overhead
edge_cases.mitigation: re-evaluate specialist advantage after every base model update; automate regression test

edge_cases.description: Concurrent write corruption: two parallel branches write to same state field simultaneously
edge_cases.trigger: parallel fan-out with shared write target in STATE_MGMT
edge_cases.mitigation: CAS or mutex on shared state writes; schema enforces write-owner per field

edge_cases.description: Router latency dominates: LLM-judge router adds more latency than specialist saves
edge_cases.trigger: router latency > accuracy gain latency equivalent
edge_cases.mitigation: profile router latency vs specialist gain; downgrade to classifier or rule router if LLM judge dominates

edge_cases.description: Join hang: parallel branch fails silently; join barrier waits indefinitely
edge_cases.trigger: branch error not propagated to join barrier
edge_cases.mitigation: barrier timeout required; failed branch emits explicit error signal not silence; circuit breaker on branch

edge_cases.description: Prompt injection chain: malicious content in external data propagates across multiple agent hops
edge_cases.trigger: external input processed by low-isolation agent; output passed unsanitized to privileged agent
edge_cases.mitigation: output sanitization at every agent boundary; privilege separation enforced at edge policy layer

edge_cases.description: Context window overflow: accumulated state exceeds consumer agent's context limit; silent truncation
edge_cases.trigger: state accumulation in STATE_MGMT exceeds model context budget
edge_cases.mitigation: state size budget enforced by schema; overflow triggers summarization to external memory tier

edge_cases.description: Conflict undetected: two agents give semantically contradictory answers that are lexically dissimilar
edge_cases.trigger: conflict detection uses lexical matching only
edge_cases.mitigation: use embedding-similarity conflict detection; LLM judge to evaluate semantic consistency

edge_cases.description: Budget exhaustion mid-graph: cost cap fires after 3 of 5 required hops; partial result returned without signal
edge_cases.trigger: cost_budget set without accounting for full graph path cost
edge_cases.mitigation: reserve full-path budget estimate before starting execution; partial result marked explicitly

edge_cases.description: Topology migration breaks in-flight executions: graph schema v2 deployed while v1 executions running
edge_cases.mitigation: versioned graph dispatch: in-flight executions complete on v1 graph; new executions on v2

edge_cases.description: Load imbalance under bursty traffic: autoscaling too slow; queue backpressure causes upstream router timeout
edge_cases.trigger: traffic burst exceeds autoscaling response time
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-warm agent pool; configure backpressure to return 429 before timeout; router applies exponential backoff

workflow.description: Specify agent roles, edge types, DAG vs cyclic policy, and termination conditions before any implementation
workflow.gate: graph passes cycle detection if DAG-only; all cycles have guards if cyclic

workflow.description: Empirically measure specialist vs generalist on production task sample; compute net value after routing overhead
workflow.gate: net value positive after routing overhead subtracted

workflow.description: Choose routing mechanism (rule/classifier/LLM-judge) based on accuracy/latency tradeoff; implement fallback
workflow.gate: router accuracy >=0.90 on held-out benchmark; fallback path tested

workflow.description: Build latency and token cost model for chosen topology; identify critical path; verify SLA feasibility
workflow.gate: modeled latency within 20% of target SLA; cost within budget

workflow.description: Implement max-iter caps, convergence checks, retry policies, and circuit breakers
workflow.gate: all cycles terminate within max_iter on adversarial inputs; retries bounded

workflow.description: Define shared state schema, write-ownership per agent, and memory tier routing policy
workflow.gate: concurrent write safety verified; state size bounded by schema

workflow.description: Implement privilege boundaries, output sanitization at agent interfaces, and audit logging
workflow.gate: injection defense tested with known payloads; privilege violations rejected

workflow.description: Set per-request and per-graph token and cost budgets; implement early-stop with explicit signal
workflow.gate: budget accounting accurate within 5%; early-stop returns partial_result signal

workflow.description: Add distributed tracing across all agent hops; configure latency dashboards and anomaly alerts
Ablate alternative topologies; compare on quality/latency/cost holding agent quality constant; select winner
workflow.gate: all metrics reported; winner selection justified by multi-metric analysis

workflow.description: Tag graph schema version; test rollback procedure in staging; deploy with versioned routing
workflow.gate: rollback procedure validated; in-flight executions not disrupted by migration

dominance_rules.rule: GRAPH_DESIGN must be finalized before ROUTER_DESIGN, LOOP_CTRL, or PARALLEL_EXEC begin implementation
dominance_rules.rationale: Routing and execution patterns are derived from graph structure; implementing without a spec creates expensive rework
dominance_rules.trigger: any implementation of routing or execution starts
dominance_rules.action: block and require GRAPH_DESIGN sign-off first

dominance_rules.rule: SPEC_BEAT evaluation must precede MoE gating or specialist routing deployment
dominance_rules.rationale: MoE and specialist routing assume specialist advantage; if advantage is not empirically validated, routing overhead is pure cost
dominance_rules.trigger: MoE or specialist routing deployment planned
dominance_rules.action: run SPEC_BEAT on production task sample; block deployment if net value negative

dominance_rules.rule: LOOP_CTRL guards required for all cycles before any cyclic topology enters staging
dominance_rules.rationale: Unbounded cycles cause infinite cost; no exception for prototypes
dominance_rules.action: require max-iter cap and timeout on all cycles before staging deployment

dominance_rules.rule: SECURITY_ISO isolation required before any any-to-any edge connects agents of different trust levels
dominance_rules.rationale: Any-to-any edges expand injection attack surface; trust boundary crossing requires sanitization
dominance_rules.action: implement and test output sanitization on the edge before deployment

dominance_rules.rule: ORCH_LATENCY model must validate SLA feasibility before topology is committed to production
dominance_rules.rationale: Post-commit latency violations are expensive to fix requiring topology rework
dominance_rules.action: run latency model; reject topology if p95 exceeds SLA target

dominance_rules.rule: COST_BOUND must reserve retry budget before FAULT_TOL retry policy is configured
dominance_rules.rationale: Retries amplify cost on degraded agents; budget without retry headroom causes budget exhaustion
dominance_rules.action: add retry_budget_fraction to total cost cap before finalizing retry policy

dominance_rules.rule: SPEC_BEAT must be re-run after every base model version increment
dominance_rules.rationale: Base model improvements may eliminate specialist advantage; failing to recheck wastes routing overhead
dominance_rules.action: trigger automated SPEC_BEAT regression; disable routing if advantage below threshold

dominance_rules.rule: STATE_MGMT concurrent write safety must be validated before PARALLEL_EXEC is enabled
dominance_rules.rationale: Parallel writes to shared state are a correctness bug not a performance concern
dominance_rules.trigger: parallel execution enabled for any branch that writes shared state
dominance_rules.action: add write-owner schema constraint and concurrency test before enabling parallel execution

dominance_rules.rule: OBS_TRACE instrumentation must achieve >=95% agent coverage before topology enters production
dominance_rules.rationale: Untraced agents make incident diagnosis impossible in production
dominance_rules.action: block on trace coverage metric; add instrumentation to uncovered agents

dominance_rules.rule: TOPO_EVAL ablation must hold agent quality constant across topology variants
dominance_rules.rationale: Comparing topologies with different agent quality conflates topology and agent effects
dominance_rules.action: pin agent model versions for all topology variants during ablation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not implement routing logic before GRAPH_DESIGN is signed off; topology changes invalidate router config
anti_rework_rules.prevents: routing rework when graph topology changes post-implementation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy specialist agents without SPEC_BEAT validation; specialist may not beat generalist on real traffic
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wasted fine-tuning and routing infrastructure cost for no accuracy gain

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not add cycles without LOOP_CTRL guards; adding guards after cycle deployment requires staged rollout
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency hotfix to add termination conditions to runaway production loops

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not configure parallel execution before STATE_MGMT write-ownership is defined; concurrent write bugs are hard to debug post-deployment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: data corruption incidents requiring state schema migration

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not set COST_BOUND budgets before ORCH_LATENCY model is calibrated; underestimated budgets cause mid-execution failures
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeated budget tuning iterations in production with user-visible partial results

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not add any-to-any edges without cycle detection check; retroactive cycle removal may require graph restructure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: topology refactor to break cycles introduced incrementally

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change STATE_MGMT schema without VERSIONING migration plan; in-flight executions break on schema change
anti_rework_rules.prevents: production incident from schema mismatch between orchestrator and agent versions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not evaluate topology variants without holding agent quality constant; topology re-selection required when quality confound discovered
anti_rework_rules.prevents: topology recommendation reversal when agent version mismatch identified

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip OBS_TRACE instrumentation for new agents; retroactive instrumentation requires redeploy
anti_rework_rules.prevents: blind incident response for uninstrumented agents

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not configure MoE gating without auxiliary load-balance loss; expert collapse recovery requires retraining
anti_rework_rules.prevents: costly expert collapse recovery requiring full MoE retraining run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not add cross-trust-tier edges without SECURITY_ISO sanitization; retroactive sanitization requires edge-by-edge audit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: security audit finding requiring emergency topology lockdown

iteration_protocol.trigger: specialist benchmark delta shrinks after base model update
iteration_protocol.action: re-run SPEC_BEAT on production task sample; disable routing if net value negative

iteration_protocol.trigger: loop runaway detected in staging or production
iteration_protocol.action: add or tighten max-iter cap in LOOP_CTRL; audit all cyclic edges in ANYANY_EDGE
increase auxiliary balance loss weight; check capacity factor in MOE_GATING; redistribute load in LOAD_BAL

iteration_protocol.trigger: latency SLA violation observed in production
iteration_protocol.action: re-run ORCH_LATENCY critical path analysis; consider topology simplification in TOPO_EVAL
tighten COST_BOUND early-stop; reduce parallel fan-out in PARALLEL_EXEC; revisit MoE gating

iteration_protocol.trigger: concurrent write corruption detected in STATE_MGMT
iteration_protocol.action: add CAS protection to affected state fields; audit all parallel write paths in PARALLEL_EXEC

iteration_protocol.trigger: prompt injection incident traced through agent chain
iteration_protocol.action: audit all any-to-any edges in SECURITY_ISO; add sanitization to affected interfaces

iteration_protocol.trigger: topology ablation reveals current topology is suboptimal
iteration_protocol.action: update GRAPH_DESIGN with new topology; re-verify ROUTER_DESIGN, LOOP_CTRL, STATE_MGMT

iteration_protocol.trigger: new agent capability added to pool
iteration_protocol.action: update ROUTER_DESIGN routes; re-run SPEC_BEAT for new capability; update LOAD_BAL pool config

iteration_protocol.trigger: trace coverage drops below 95% after agent deployment
iteration_protocol.action: add instrumentation to new agents in OBS_TRACE; verify trace propagation across async boundaries

priority_rationale: GRAPH_DESIGN first as all other work depends on topology; SPEC_BEAT second to validate specialist assumption before investing in routing; ROUTER_DESIGN and LOOP_CTRL next as they gate execution correctness; SECURITY_ISO before any-to-any edges; ORCH_LATENCY and COST_BOUND gate production viability; STATE_MGMT before PARALLEL_EXEC to prevent concurrency bugs; evaluation and versioning last as they depend on implementation artifacts

all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all conflict_axis_refs in nodes resolve to valid CA ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true

observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
all derived fields set to 0 (pre-formula run)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
